title: Cooking rice and pasta
examples: How much water should I use for rice?
What is the difference between boiling and simmering?
What does it mean if pasta is cooked al dente?

explain.say: Today we learn how to cook rice and pasta well. We must learn about water ratios first.
Next we need to know about boiling water. Boiling means the water is very hot. You must bring the water to a rolling boil.
We cook pasta by adding it to the boiling water. You cook it for a set time to get it soft.
Al dente means cooked but still firm to the bite. This is a perfect texture for many pasta dishes.
For rice, you usually boil the water first. Then you add the rice and let it cook gently.
In real life, when making soup, you must boil the water first. Then you add the vegetables and let it simmer.

faq.q: What is the best water ratio for rice?
faq.a: For most white rice, use a ratio of one part rice to two parts water. This helps the rice absorb moisture evenly. You could also ask, 'How much water to rice?' or 'What is the rice water ratio?'
asks: What is the water to rice ratio?

faq.q: What does 'al dente' mean when cooking pasta?
faq.a: Al dente means that the pasta is cooked until it is firm to the bite, but not hard. This texture is preferred by many chefs. You might also ask, 'Is al dente too soft?' or 'What is the right pasta texture?'
asks: How firm should cooked pasta be?

faq.q: Do I boil the water or just bring it to a boil?
faq.a: You must bring the water to a rolling boil before adding pasta or rice. Boiling means the water has reached its maximum temperature. You could ask, 'How hot should the water be?' or 'Do I just heat the water?'
asks: How do I know when water is boiling?
Should I just heat the water?

faq.q: Is there a different ratio for different types of rice?
faq.a: Yes, some types of rice, like brown rice, might need a slightly different ratio. Always check the specific cooking instructions on the package. You could ask, 'Does rice type matter for water?' or 'What about brown rice ratio?'
asks: Does the rice type change the water amount?

faq.q: What is the difference between boiling and simmering?
faq.a: Boiling means the water has large, rapid bubbles breaking the surface. Simmering means the water is gently hot with small bubbles breaking occasionally. You could ask, 'What is the difference between boiling and simmering?' or 'Can I simmer rice?'

facts: Rice typically uses a water ratio of one part to two parts.
Boiling water means it is at its highest temperature.
Al dente means firm to the bite, not mushy.
Pasta should be cooked in plenty of boiling water.

quiz.say: If a recipe says use 1 cup of rice to 2 cups of water, what is the ratio?
quiz.why: The ratio is one part rice to two parts water, which is 1:2.

wrong.1: This is wrong because it suggests too much water for the amount of rice.
wrong.2: This is wrong because it means the water and rice are equal, which is usually too little water.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the standard ratio is simpler and uses less water.

quiz.say: When cooking pasta, what does 'al dente' describe?
quiz.why: Al dente means it is cooked through but still has a slight firmness.

wrong.0: This means the pasta was not cooked enough at all.
wrong.1: This describes the water level, not the texture of the pasta.
wrong.3: This describes overcooked pasta, which loses its shape.

quiz.say: If you are cooking rice, what must happen before you add the rice?
quiz.why: You must bring the water to a boil to ensure the rice cooks properly and evenly.

wrong.0: Boiling the rice directly can make it sticky or unevenly cooked.
wrong.2: Adding rice to cold water will make the cooking process take too long.
wrong.3: Steaming might not provide enough direct heat for the water ratio to work.
